title: GlassPane updater state (spec 2026-09-27 §4)
description: Shape of <stateRoot>/update-state.json and of the single JSON line `--json` prints. Validated inside this package only: it is local installation state, not a cross-language evidence contract, so it deliberately does NOT live in kernel/schemas.

caRoots.description: What happened the last time this machine exported a system root bundle for node. Node reads NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS when a process starts and never consults the macOS trust store, so on a machine whose TLS is intercepted by a locally trusted root (corporate gateway, accelerator) an updater without this bundle fails its first network gate every single day while looking exactly like a working agent. Only `ok` is usable; every other status is read together with the remedy §9 of the auto-update spec attaches. Deliberately absent from `required`: a state file written before this existed must still load, and absent/null means 'this install never exported one', never 'fine'.

runtime.description: Spec 11: whether the updater's own installed copy moved with this swap. The daily job runs the code that update-install.json's updaterCli names, while 3.5 swaps the .app bundles and the npm packages, so a release whose content is 'fix the updater' reaches a machine only if this record says refreshed. Absent or null means this install has never gone through a swap that tried: it is not evidence that the updater is current. `status` is a closed vocabulary; a reader that cannot match it must report 'unreadable', never fall back to refreshed. agentVerified is true only after the loaded launchd job was read back and names the new script.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant this file was published.

lastCheckAt.description: ISO-8601 instant of the last check that reached the source, or null when nothing has ever been checked. Drives the 36 h overdue judgement.

current.description: Version the machine is running, read back from the installed bundle.

latest.description: Highest version the source offered, parseable tag stripped of its v.

code.description: Stable code of the gate that refused, or null. The panel switches on this, never on the message text.

authorship.description: Gate 8: how the source of the release this record is about was established. Written by `check` the moment the signature gate is reached, and it outlives `staged` on purpose: after a successful apply this is the only thing on disk that still says the installed release came without authorship proof. `consented: true` means a person passed --consent unsigned-release, i.e. accepted the missing proof; the scheduled run cannot. `signature-tool-missing` means this machine could not check at all (no gpg, or no key to check against). Deliberately absent from `required`: a state file written before gate 8 must still load, and a document that cannot be read is a machine that cannot update.

message.description: Human-actionable sentence. No internal section numbers, no self-justification.
